answer:
The total sum of the original 20 observations is

\[
20\cdot 14=280.
\]

Let \(L\) be the largest observation and \(S\) the smallest.

After removing \(L\), the 19 remaining observations have mean \(12\), so their sum is

\[
19\cdot 12=228.
\]

Thus

\[
L=280-228=52.
\]

After removing \(S\), the 19 remaining observations have mean \(14.5\), so their sum is

\[
19\cdot 14.5=275.5.
\]

Thus

\[
S=280-275.5=4.5.
\]

Therefore the range is

\[
L-S=52-4.5=47.5.
\]

So the range is

\[
\boxed{47.5}.
\]

Could every observation have been an integer?  
No. If all observations were integers, then removing the smallest integer would leave a sum of 19 integers, which must be an integer. But

\[
19\cdot 14.5=275.5
\]

is not an integer. Equivalently, the smallest observation would have to be \(4.5\), which is not an integer. Hence not every observation could have been an integer.

\[
\boxed{\text{Range }=47.5,\quad \text{not all observations can be integers.}}
\]
